thesis: The +27% 60-day rebound off the Oct 30 52-week low ($225) isn't tied to any confirmed company-disclosed catalyst in this run's research. A securities class action (N.D. Cal.) alleging AppLovin misled investors about its AI ad platform has its lead-plaintiff deadline today, Nov 16. Reports conflict on whether an SEC probe is still open: the CFO said in August that one was closed, but October reports describe a new or ongoing one. A separate San Diego children's-data suit is also pending. This suggests the rebound may be sentiment-driven while the legal overhang remains unresolved.
invalidation: Confirmed closure of all SEC inquiries plus a company-disclosed fundamental catalyst (e.g. guidance raise) that explains the rebound

thesis: The +15% 60-day run-up comes right before the confirmed Q3 report tomorrow (Nov 17, before the open). Options imply a ±7.1% move, against a 3.9% ten-year average. The last quarter beat ($4.92 vs $4.71), but flat comparable-sales guidance, lower operating margins, acquisition costs and housing pressure remain open concerns. The setup is mixed, and an unresolved binary event lands within a day, so taking a position ahead of the print isn't supported.
invalidation: Q3 print beats and raises comp/margin guidance, clearing the housing-pressure concern

thesis: PG is at a 52-week high ($173.14 vs $173.57) after a +15% 60-day move. Coverage credits productivity-savings disclosures and a break above the 200-day SMA, which suggests investors are re-rating defensive staples with company-specific cost execution behind it. The next company-specific catalyst, P&G Investor Day on Nov 19, is still pending, and this run found no scheduled litigation event or governance issue.
invalidation: Investor Day (Nov 19) targets disappoint, or price closes back below the 200-day SMA

thesis: LLY is up 25% over 60 days and sits 2.8% below a fresh 52-week high. Reported drivers are a Q3 beat with full-year revenue guidance raised for the third time this year (Reuters via Finimize: shares hit a record) and the FDA approval and launch of oral GLP-1 Foundayo (orforglipron), which also succeeded in the ACHIEVE-4 CV trial. The strongest counter-case is competition from Novo's oral Wegovy plus a rich ~47x P/E. The repeated guidance raises suggest demand is absorbing that so far. However, this run could not pin the exact date or figures of the Q3 2026 release, so the catalyst confirmation is incomplete. No scheduled litigation or governance event was found.
invalidation: Guidance cut, Foundayo launch uptake materially below expectations, or a safety signal on the GLP-1 franchise

thesis: Visa is up 15% over 60 days and 3.5% below its Nov 5 52-week high, but this run's search found no confirmed November company-specific catalyst behind the move. The DOJ debit-monopolization suit (S.D.N.Y., filed Sep 2024) is still open, and no scheduled ruling or trial date within 90 days surfaced, so it isn't flagged. Visa calls the suit meritless. With no identified catalyst and the antitrust case unresolved, the evidence doesn't reach a clear net read.
invalidation: Adverse ruling or remedy in the DOJ debit case, or a payment-volume slowdown in the next report

thesis: SKHY is down 28% over 60 days and sits at a new 52-week low ($122.17 vs $121.94). It fell about 13.4% on Nov 5 in a broad semiconductor selloff, alongside reports that the US Commerce Department keeps holding up equipment export licenses for its China NAND plants. Much of the drawdown looks like sector-wide memory/AI sentiment rather than a disclosed company deterioration. A counterpoint: roughly half of 2027-28 capacity is reportedly already contracted. The ADR listed in July 2026 and has only 90 real daily bars, so the trend filter was skipped.
invalidation: Export licenses granted and memory pricing/AI capex sentiment stabilizes with price reclaiming the post-IPO range

thesis: SPCX is down 10.1% over 60 days, barely past the threshold. It is a June 2026 IPO with only 108 real daily bars (trend filter skipped) and a reported beta of about 4.6. This run found no November company-specific catalyst. Recent headlines are a Tesla merger that needs Musk's approval and an executive share donation, neither of which resolves the direction. The move looks sentiment-driven, and price swings are extreme.
invalidation: A confirmed company-disclosed catalyst (e.g. merger terms, Starlink results) plus stabilization above the IPO-era range

thesis: CGON jumped 13.5% today on 8.3x average volume to a new 52-week high after positive topline results from the company's Phase 3 PIVOT-006 trial. Cretostimogene cut recurrence risk by 68% vs surveillance (HR 0.32, n=367) in intermediate-risk NMIBC. That supports a second BLA (Q2 2027), and the BCG-unresponsive BLA expansion is now expected by end of March 2027. The trial result is a confirmed company disclosure, but detailed data at SUO on Dec 2 is a pending event that could still shift the read, and commercialization is well over a year out. Earlier coverage cited about $903M liquidity, and no offering, litigation or governance issue surfaced.
invalidation: Detailed PIVOT-006 data at SUO (Dec 2) shows weaker durability or safety issues, or an equity raise is announced

thesis: INGM traded 4.6x average volume today while falling 3.1%. Principal stockholder Platinum Equity priced an 11M-share secondary at $25.90 on Nov 2, with Goldman as sole underwriter holding a 30-day option on about 1.65M more shares. This follows earlier 2026 secondaries in March and May. Concurrent company buybacks (1M shares) partly offset this. The repeated sponsor selling suggests a continuing supply overhang rather than a fundamental catalyst, and this run found no company-disclosed operating news.
invalidation: Sponsor sell-down completes and the next earnings report shows margin/revenue upside

thesis: Held position. COST is at a 52-week high ($1114.42; the high of $1117.00 was set today) after a +23.7% 60-day move. The driver is company-disclosed October sales: net sales up 12.6% to $24.50B, with total comps up 7.3% excluding gas and FX effects. The strongest counter-case is valuation (about 45x forward P/E vs about 30x for the industry) and gas inflation flattering reported growth by about 3.9 points. Even excluding gas, comps of 7.3% show the underlying demand trend is real, so the counter-case doesn't change the read. The next binary event is Q1 FY27 earnings on Dec 10, weeks after the next review. No litigation or governance flags surfaced.
invalidation: Ex-gas comps decelerate below ~4% in the November sales report, or Q1 margins disappoint on Dec 10
